attributes.translation: (Someone said) that person will give me a small puppy. (I will be given)
attributes.nuance_translation: A structure used when (A) is being given to the speaker, or someone in their in-group, from somebody else.

attributes.body:
くれる is generally taught as part of a set of 3 verbs that are regularly used for giving and receiving in Japanese. These verbs are くれる, あげる, and もらう. くれる means 'to give' (to you, or someone that is part of your 'in' group).

With くれる and あげる, they both function in the regular way you would expect (regarding particles). This means that が will always mark the giver (the person performing the action), and に will mark the recipient (the person that is the 'destination' of the thing that is given). This means that を will be used to mark the 'object' that is given, as is usually the case.

The giver/recipient are often omitted from sentences with くれる, as one/both are usually obvious from context, or the sentence may be focusing on the object.

As can be seen here, the same nuance is kept, even when things are omitted.

Fun Fact

What someone considers their 'in' group will be different for each person, but usually consists of members of your family, clubs that you are in, or something similar that has a 'group' atmosphere (that you are a part of).

The giver will always be someone that is more distant than the people that are in the 'group'.

Caution

When we want to say that we (or someone else) gave something to someone that is not in our 'in' group, we will need to use あげる instead.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Inner/outer circles and which verb to use
あげる, くれる, and もらう as Verbs

attributes.body: くれる means 'to give' and is used when someone outside the speaker's group gives something to the speaker or their in-group. For example, プレゼントをくれた means '(someone) gave me a present.' As てくれる, it shows someone did something for the speaker's benefit, as in 日本語を教えてくれた ('(someone) taught me Japanese').

second_relatable.title: てくれる
second_relatable.meaning: To do something for someone (usually you)

attributes.body: あげる and くれる are basic verbs for giving. あげる is used when the speaker or their in-group gives something to someone outside the group, or when one out-group member gives to another. くれる is used when someone outside the speaker's group gives something to the speaker or their in-group. In both cases, the subject marked by が is the giver.

first_relatable.title: あげる
first_relatable.meaning: To give (away), To present, To provide

attributes.body: くれる means 'to give' and is used when someone from the speaker's out-group gives something to the speaker or their in-group. The subject, marked with が, is the giver. In contrast, もらう means 'to receive' and describes the action from the receiver's perspective. With もらう, the subject marked with が is the one receiving.

first_relatable.title: もらう
first_relatable.meaning: To receive, To get, To obtain

attributes.body: くれる is a basic verb meaning 'to give,' usually used when someone from outside the speaker's group gives something to the speaker or their in-group. For example, プレゼントをくれた means '(someone) gave me a present.' It also appears in the pattern てくれてありがとう to thank someone for a favor. For example, 日本語を教えてくれてありがとう means 'Thank you for teaching me Japanese.'
